name: Adaptive Convergence Threshold
definition: A convergence criterion where the ray stops when the absolute SDF is smaller than a threshold $\epsilon$. The threshold is calculated based on camera parameters to ensure balls centered at ray front ends of neighboring pixels do not intersect.
summary: Adaptive Convergence Threshold is a camera-aware stopping condition for ray marching that prevents geometric dilation and erosion by adapting the convergence epsilon to camera intrinsics and scene scale.
